All these routes involve considerable indirection to General Mitchell Field leaving a more direct and higher type facility to travel on more desirable.
Additionally, the airport can be considered as a major denerator of traffic and the impact becomes significant when considered in terms of traffic on the existing local street system in the vicinity of the airport and the funneling of this traffic into the airport entrance road. The projected traffic volumes and related congestion, accidents, noise and air pollution indicate that alternate routing of airport oriented traffic will be not only desirable but necessary.
Recent field studies indicate the complete dominance of the automobile as the major mode of transportation destined to the airport. At the present time more than 90% of all vehicles entering the passenger terminal area of General Mitchell Field are private cars. The remaining 10% are comprised of buses, taxis and airport limousines. The automobile will remain as the principal mode of transportation in the foreseeable future. The rubber tired transit system of buses using the existing freeway system will be secondary because of the diversity in trip origin-destination.
